checks.title: Balances add up to the files the banks sent
checks.plain: Every balance on this page, added together, equals the two banks' files to the cent.
checks.sql:
SELECT round((SELECT sum(CAST(CUR_BAL_CENTS AS BIGINT)) / 100.0 FROM raw_a_accounts) + (SELECT sum(balance) FROM raw_b_accounts), 2) AS raw_total,
                    round((SELECT sum(balance) FROM account_360), 2) AS gold_total
checks.detail: Harbor Bank cents / 100 plus Riverside Bank dollars versus the sum of account_360.balance

checks.title: Every account belongs to a known person
checks.plain: No account is floating without a customer behind it.
checks.sql: SELECT count(*) FROM account_360 a LEFT JOIN customer_360 c USING (customer_key) WHERE c.customer_key IS NULL OR a.customer_key IS NULL

checks.title: Every transaction belongs to a known account
checks.plain: No money moved on an account we cannot find.
checks.sql:
SELECT count(*) FROM transactions t LEFT JOIN account_360 a ON a.source_system = t.source_system AND a.source_account_id = t.source_account_id
             WHERE a.source_account_id IS NULL OR t.customer_key IS NULL

checks.title: Nobody is listed twice
checks.plain: Each bank record was used once, and a customer key is shared only by the two records of one matched person.
checks.sql:
SELECT (SELECT count(*) - count(DISTINCT source_system || ':' || source_customer_id) FROM customer_xref)
                  + (SELECT count(*) FROM (
                        SELECT customer_key, count(*) AS records, count(matched_with) AS matched, count(DISTINCT source_system) AS systems
                        FROM customer_xref GROUP BY 1)
                     WHERE records > 1 AND NOT (records = 2 AND matched = 2 AND systems = 2))
                  + (SELECT count(*) - count(DISTINCT customer_key) FROM customer_360)
checks.detail: Counts source records used twice, keys held by records that are not one matched Core A + Core B pair, and duplicate customer_360 keys

checks.title: Every number can be traced to its source
checks.plain: Every column on this page names the bank system it came from, the field, and the rule applied, in plain words.

checks.title: The matching made no wrong merges
checks.plain: Checked against the answer key: 265 merges, 0 wrong, 0 of the same-name traps fooled it.

checks.title: Transactions fall inside the year of data
checks.plain: All transactions are dated within the 365 days before the as-of date, 2026-09-30.
checks.sql: SELECT count(*), min(txn_ts), max(txn_ts) FROM transactions WHERE txn_ts < TIMESTAMP '2026-09-30' - INTERVAL 365 DAY OR txn_ts > TIMESTAMP '2026-09-30' + INTERVAL 1 DAY

checks.title: 'Quiet' means what it says
checks.plain: An account is flagged quiet exactly when it is open and the transaction list shows nothing in the 180 days before the as-of date, never otherwise.
checks.sql:
SELECT count(*) FROM account_360 a
             LEFT JOIN (SELECT source_system, source_account_id, max(txn_ts) AS last_ts FROM transactions GROUP BY 1, 2) t
                    USING (source_system, source_account_id)
             WHERE a.is_dormant_180d != (a.is_open AND (t.last_ts IS NULL OR t.last_ts < TIMESTAMP '2026-09-30 23:59:59.999999' - INTERVAL 180 DAY))
checks.detail: Recomputed from max(txn_ts) per account in the exported transactions, independently of account_360.txn_count_180d

checks.title: People keep the same key from one month to the next
checks.plain: This is the first load, so there is no earlier month to compare against yet.
checks.detail: Evaluated from the second batch onwards

checks.title: A person's 'quiet checking' flag matches their accounts
checks.plain: A person is marked as having a quiet checking account exactly when at least one of their open checking accounts is quiet.
checks.sql:
SELECT count(*) FROM customer_360 c
             LEFT JOIN (SELECT customer_key, bool_or(is_dormant_180d) AS any_dormant FROM account_360
                        WHERE is_open AND product_type = 'checking' GROUP BY 1) a USING (customer_key)
             WHERE c.checking_dormant_180d != coalesce(a.any_dormant, false)
checks.detail: customer_360.checking_dormant_180d versus bool_or(account_360.is_dormant_180d) over open checking accounts
